mainTopic: The זב's fluids, a dried or burnt שרץ, טומאה only when moist, and retroactive טומאה from a שרץ or a כתם
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: a זב's urine is טמא because of the word "וזאת", since logic fails when blood from the same place is טהור. The word "הוא" teaches that the blood is טהור. To explain why urine is included and blood excluded, רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי says the impure fluids are like רוק: they gather, come out, and can be reabsorbed. This rule also excludes a woman's milk. רבא explains that זוב itself cannot serve as a model, because it is unique. The גמרא then turns to the שרץ. ריש לקיש rules that a dried or burnt שרץ with an intact skeleton is still טמא. רבי זירא defends him by splitting whole from partial, backed by a ברייתא on the words "בהם" and "מהם". The גמרא then gives sources for why the items in the משנה are טמא only when moist, discusses soaking dried items in lukewarm water, and has שמואל explain that dried corpse flesh still carries טומאת רקב. A new משנה teaches that a שרץ found in an alleyway or a כתם found on a garment makes things טמא back to the last check or cleaning. The גמרא begins asking why sweeping counts as a cutoff.

steps.title: A logical argument that urine should be impure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that a זב's urine should be טמא because it comes from the same impure place as his זוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes from an impure place, so isn't it logical that it should be impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא (which started before this section) offers a logical reason why a זב's urine should be טמא. It is setting up an argument that the next line will knock down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is simple: the urine comes out of the same opening as the זוב, which is a source of טומאה. So you would expect anything coming from there to be טמא too.

keyTerms.meaning: An impure place, here the opening that the זוב comes from
Isn't it logical? A formula that introduces a reasoned argument

phrases.english: From a place of impurity,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is talking about a זב's urine, which comes from the same place as his זוב.

phrases.english: is it not logical that they should be impure?

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Logic suggests that urine, which comes from the place of זוב, should be טמא.

steps.title: Blood from the same place proves the logic fails
steps.stepSummary: Blood from the opening of the penis comes from the same impure place, yet it is טהור. So urine could also be טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood that comes out of the opening of the penis proves otherwise. It comes from an impure place and is still pure. So don't be surprised if urine, though it comes from an impure place, is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down its own logical argument by pointing to blood, which comes from the same place but is טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule "anything from an impure place is impure" is shown to be false, because blood breaks it. Once that rule falls, there is no logical proof left that urine is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (it wrong). A counter-example that breaks an argument
The opening of the male organ

phrases.english: Blood that comes out of the opening of the penis will prove otherwise,
for it comes from an impure place, and yet it is pure.

phrases.aramaic: אַף אַתָּה אַל תִּתְמַהּ עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: So you too should not be surprised about this,
phrases.notes: "This" means the urine.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבָּא מִמְּקוֹם טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: that even though it comes from a place of impurity
it should be pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the logical argument of step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The logical proof that urine is טמא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Coming from an impure place does not guarantee טומאה, as blood shows.

steps.title: The verse includes urine in impurity
steps.stepSummary: Since logic doesn't work, the פסוק "וזאת" is needed to include a זב's urine in severe טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says "His issue is impure... and this" to include his urine in impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא concludes that a זב's urine is טמא because the פסוק includes it, not because of logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "וזאת" is read as a ריבוי, a word that adds something. Here it adds urine to the fluids of a זב that are טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches. Introduces a source from a פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: A זב's urine is טמא with severe טומאה, learned from the word "וזאת". Logic alone could not prove it, because blood from the same place is טהור.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "His issue is impure... and this" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:2–3

phrases.english: to include his urine for impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק after the logical route failed
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A זב's urine carries severe טומאה, based on the ריבוי of "וזאת".

steps.title: How do we know the blood is pure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that blood from the opening of the penis is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood that comes out of the opening of the penis: from where do we know it is pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא relied on the fact that this blood is טהור. Now the גמרא asks where that fact comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument in step 2 depended on the blood being טהור. The גמרא wants a source for that assumption.

phrases.english: Blood that comes out of the opening of the penis,
from where do we know that it is pure?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that blood from the opening of the penis is טהור

steps.title: The word 'it' excludes blood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "זובו טמא הוא" that only the זוב is טמא, so blood from the mouth or the penis is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: you might think blood from his mouth or from the opening of the penis is impure. So the verse says "His issue, it is impure": it is impure, but blood from his mouth or from the penis is not impure. Rather, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads the word "הוא" ("it") as limiting טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הוא" is read as a מיעוט, a word that excludes. It limits the טומאה to the זוב itself and its included fluids, so blood from the mouth or the penis is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think. Introduces a possibility that the verse will reject
It. Read here as excluding other fluids

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
One might think that blood that comes out
from his mouth or from the opening of the penis is impure?
The verse says: "His issue, it is impure" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:2

phrases.english: it is impure,
but blood that comes out of his mouth
or from the opening of the penis is not impure; rather, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מיעוט "הוא" excludes blood from the mouth and the penis from טומאה.

steps.title: Why not flip the two דרשות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't use "וזאת" to include blood and "הוא" to exclude urine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let me reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: Now we have one word that includes ("וזאת") and one word that excludes ("הוא"). The גמרא challenges how we know which fluid goes with which word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the words themselves says that urine is included and blood is excluded. The opposite assignment seems just as possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me reverse it. A challenge that swaps two rulings

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not against the דרשות themselves. It only asks which fluid gets which דרשה.

phrases.english: But let me reverse it!
phrases.notes: He means: use "וזאת" to include blood, and "הוא" to exclude urine.

steps.kashyaTarget: The way the two דרשות were assigned to urine and blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse words don't specify which fluid is included and which is excluded, so the assignment could be flipped.

steps.title: Like saliva: fluids that gather and then come out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: the impure fluids are like רוק, which gathers and then comes out. Urine fits this; blood does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: it is like saliva. Just as saliva gathers and then comes out, so too anything that gathers and then comes out is included. This excludes blood, which does not gather and come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The included fluid must be similar to רוק, and urine is similar while blood is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רוק of a זב is a known source of טומאה, so it sets the model. Fluids that collect and then exit fit that model, so urine is included by "וזאת". Blood flows without collecting first, so it is the fluid excluded by "הוא".

keyTerms.meaning: Gathers together and then comes out

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the rule for which bodily fluids of a זב carry severe טומאה: those that gather and then come out, like רוק.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
It is similar to saliva:
just as saliva gathers together and then comes out,
so too anything that gathers together and then comes out.
This excludes blood,
which does not gather together and then come out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי דּוּמְיָא דְּרוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the איפוך אנא challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The included and excluded fluids could be swapped.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only fluids that gather and then come out, like רוק, are included, so urine is טמא and blood is טהור.

steps.title: Challenge from a woman's milk
steps.stepSummary: A woman's milk gathers and then comes out, yet it carries only טומאת משקין, not severe טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a woman's milk, which gathers and then comes out. And the Master said: a woman's milk makes things impure with the impurity of liquids. The impurity of liquids, yes, but not severe impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule with a case that seems to break it: a woman's milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every fluid that gathers and comes out carries severe טומאה like רוק, milk should too. But a known teaching says milk carries only the lighter טומאת משקין, so the rule seems too broad. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is... Introduces a counter-example
The impurity of liquids, a lighter level of טומאה
Severe impurity, like the רוק of a זב

phrases.english: But there is a woman's milk,
which gathers together and then comes out,
and the Master said:
A woman's milk makes things impure with the impurity of liquids.
The impurity of liquids, yes,
but not severe impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just given in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that whatever gathers and comes out carries severe טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Milk gathers and comes out, yet it carries only טומאת משקין, so the rule seems to fail.

steps.title: The saliva model, refined: gathers, comes out, and can be reabsorbed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי adds a condition. The fluid must also be able to go back into the body, like רוק. This excludes blood and a woman's milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: it must be like saliva. Saliva gathers, comes out, and can be swallowed back. So every impure fluid must gather, come out, and be able to go back in. Blood is excluded, because it does not gather first. A woman's milk is excluded, because even though it gathers and comes out, it cannot go back in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the answer from step 7 so that it no longer includes a woman's milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 the problem was that milk also gathers and comes out, yet it carries only טומאת משקין. So a second condition is added: the fluid must also be able to be reabsorbed. Milk fails this condition, and blood still fails the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: Saliva, the model fluid for this rule
Gathers together and then comes out
Goes back and is absorbed or swallowed again

steps.whatToRemember: Severe טומאה applies only to a fluid that, like רוק, (1) gathers, (2) comes out, and (3) can go back in. Blood fails test 1. Milk fails test 3.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
It is like saliva:
just as saliva gathers and comes out,
and can go back and be swallowed again,
so too, anything that gathers and comes out,
and can go back and be absorbed again.
This excludes blood,
which does not gather and then come out.
This excludes a woman's milk,
for even though it gathers and comes out,
it does not go back and get absorbed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the milk challenge of step 8 by refining the rule from step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a further condition to the defining rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any fluid that gathers and comes out carries severe טומאה, which would wrongly include milk
steps.terutzMaskana: The fluid must also be able to be reabsorbed, so milk is excluded

steps.title: Challenge: learn from זוב that even non-gathering fluids are טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that זוב itself does not gather before coming out, yet it is טמא. So why not make all fluids טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from 'his זוב': just as his זוב does not gather and come out, yet it makes things טמא, so too all fluids should.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the saliva rule using זוב itself as a counter-example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saliva rule says that only gathering fluids are severely טמא. But זוב is the main impure fluid, and it does not gather. So זוב could serve as a model for including blood and milk too.

keyTerms.meaning: His זוב, the discharge that makes a man a זב

phrases.english: But let us learn from "his discharge":
phrases.notes: This is the word from the פסוק "זובו טמא הוא" quoted in step 5 (ויקרא 15:2).

phrases.english: just as "his discharge" does not gather and come out
and yet it makes things impure, so too all fluids!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the saliva model from step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: זוב does not gather, yet it is טמא, so gathering should not be required

steps.title: רבא: זוב is unique because it creates טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that זוב cannot be a model, because it has a special power: it makes the person himself a זב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: you cannot learn from 'his זוב', because it causes טומאה to others.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא blocks the comparison by showing that זוב is in a class of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זוב is what turns a man into a זב in the first place. Other fluids do not create that status. A fluid with such a unique power cannot be used as a model to include ordinary fluids like blood or milk.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible to learn from it
Causes טומאה to others; here, it makes the person a זב

phrases.english: Rava said:
From "his discharge" one cannot learn,
since it causes impurity to others.
phrases.notes: "Others" here means the man who sees it: the זוב is what makes him a זב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the source case as unique
steps.terutzHavaAmina: זוב can be a model for all fluids
steps.terutzMaskana: זוב has a special stringency, so the saliva rule stands
steps.whatToRemember: The saliva rule stands. זוב is a special case because it creates the זב status itself.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a dried שרץ with an intact skeleton is טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the משנה's word 'and the שרץ'. ריש לקיש rules that a dried שרץ whose skeleton remains whole is still טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'and the שרץ'. ריש לקיש said: a שרץ that dried up but whose skeleton is still intact is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. The גמרא quotes the שרץ from the משנה and brings ריש לקיש's ruling about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the שרץ among things that make others טמא only when moist. ריש לקיש adds that a dried שרץ is still טמא if its skeleton stays whole. This sets up the clash in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the eight creeping creatures whose dead body is טמא
Its skeleton or frame remains intact

phrases.english: "And the creeping animal."
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from the משנה, which lists things that make others impure only when moist.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
"A creeping animal that dried up but its skeleton is intact" is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dried שרץ with its skeleton intact is טמא

steps.title: The משנה says dry ones are not טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש from the משנה, which says these items make others טמא only when moist, not when dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: they make things טמא when moist, and they do not make things טמא when dry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the משנה against ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to say that any dry שרץ is טהור. ריש לקיש says a dry שרץ can be טמא. These two statements look like a direct contradiction.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the משנה:
they make things impure when moist
and do not make things impure when dry!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש from step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says a dry שרץ is not טמא at all

steps.title: רבי זירא: whole skeleton versus partial
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that ריש לקיש speaks of a שרץ that is entirely whole, while the משנה speaks of only part of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: it is not difficult. This one (ריש לקיש) is talking about the whole of it. That one (the משנה) is talking about part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא settles the contradiction by assigning each source to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dried שרץ with its whole frame still intact stays טמא, which is ריש לקיש's case. When only part of it is there, it makes things טמא only while moist, which is the משנה's case. So the two sources do not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources fit together
All of it; the complete creature

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: It is not difficult.
This one is about the whole of it,
phrases.notes: "This one" is ריש לקיש's ruling: the dried שרץ is still all there.

phrases.english: that one is about part of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ריש לקיש contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: A whole dried שרץ is טמא, while a partial one is טמא only when moist

steps.title: A ברייתא: the Torah speaks of both the whole and part of a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי shows that the פסוקים treat a whole שרץ and part of a שרץ as two separate cases. This supports רבי זירא's split.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יצחק son of רבי ביסנא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: 'them' might mean only all of it, so the Torah says 'of them', meaning even part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי זירא's distinction between a whole שרץ and part of one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בהם' could suggest that only a complete שרץ is טמא. The word 'מהם' teaches that even part of a שרץ is טמא. Since the Torah itself separates the whole from the part, it makes sense that each one has its own rules, as רבי זירא said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Them'; might suggest only the whole creature (ויקרא 11:31)
'Of them'; teaches that even part counts (ויקרא 11:32)

steps.whatToRemember: A whole dried שרץ stays טמא. Part of a שרץ is also a source of טומאה, but only while moist. The Torah's words 'בהם' and 'מהם' point to these two cases.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Bisna said,
Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said:
"Them": one might think it means only all of it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:31

phrases.english: so the verse says "of them."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:32. "Of them" means even a piece of the שרץ counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי זירא's distinction from step 14
steps.raayaObject: The split between a whole שרץ and part of a שרץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי on 'בהם' and 'מהם'

steps.title: The ברייתא resolves the two verses: moist versus dry
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes. 'Of them' alone would include a part of a שרץ, and 'them' alone would require a whole one. So a moist שרץ makes things טמא even when only part of it is there, and a dry שרץ makes things טמא only when it is whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we had only the word 'of them', we might think even part of a שרץ makes things טמא. That is why the verse also says 'them'. How do the two fit together? One verse speaks of a moist שרץ, and the other speaks of a dry one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי from step 15. The ברייתא shows how the two verses fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word on its own would point in a different direction: 'of them' suggests even a part counts, and 'them' suggests only a whole one counts. The ברייתא keeps both. A moist שרץ makes things טמא even when only part of it is there, but a dry שרץ does so only when it is whole. This is how the ברייתא backs up the whole-versus-part split from step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (it says this word to rule out a mistaken idea)
How is this so? (how do the two sources fit together)

steps.whatToRemember: Moist שרץ: even part of it is טמא. Dry שרץ: only a whole one is טמא.

phrases.english: If [we had only] 'of them' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:32

phrases.english: one might think it applies even to part of them,
so the verse says 'them'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:31

phrases.english: How is this so?
Here — with a moist one; there — with a dry one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? כָּאן — בְּלַח, כָּאן — בְּיָבֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's split between a whole שרץ and part of a שרץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, reading 'בהם' and 'מהם' (ויקרא 11:31-32)

steps.title: Dried lizards of מחוזא with an intact skeleton are טמא
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the lizards of מחוזא are טמא when their skeleton is intact.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: These lizards of מחוזא are טמא when their skeleton is still whole.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a practical ruling about dried-out lizards found in his city, מחוזא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lizard is one of the שרצים. Even when it has dried out, an intact skeleton still counts as a 'whole' שרץ, which fits the rule that a dry שרץ is טמא only when whole.

phrases.english: רבא said:
These lizards of מחוזא,
when their skeleton is intact — they are טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the dry-but-whole rule to a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dried lizards with an intact skeleton are טמא.

steps.title: A burnt שרץ with an intact skeleton is טמא
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that a שרץ that was burned is still טמא if its skeleton is intact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: A שרץ that was burned, but whose skeleton is still whole, is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling of ריש לקיש: even a burnt שרץ stays טמא as long as its skeleton holds together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning is harsher than drying out, but ריש לקיש says the same rule applies. If the skeleton is intact, the שרץ still counts as whole, and so it is טמא. This ruling sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure, and passes on impurity

phrases.english: And ריש לקיש said:
A שרץ that was burned
and its skeleton is intact — is טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of ריש לקיש, parallel to his dried-שרץ ruling in step 12, now about a burnt שרץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A burnt שרץ with an intact skeleton is טמא.

steps.title: A משנה says a burnt שרץ found on olives leaves them טהור
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that a burnt שרץ found on olives does not make them טמא, because we judge impurity by its state when it is found. This seems to contradict ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: If a burnt שרץ was found on top of olives, and likewise a worn-out rag, they are טהור. This is because all impurities are judged by how they are at the moment they are found!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש with a משנה that treats a burnt שרץ as unable to make things טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says we do not worry that the שרץ touched the olives before it was burned. We look at it as it is now, and as it is now, burnt, it does not make things טמא. That seems to say a burnt שרץ is not טמא, against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their state at the time they are found

phrases.english: They challenged him:

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא שֶׁרֶץ שָׂרוּף עַל גַּבֵּי הַזֵּיתִים,
phrases.english: If a burnt שרץ was found on top of the olives,
and likewise a worn-out rag — they are טהור,
because all impurities are judged as they are at the time they are found!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: נִמְצָא שֶׁרֶץ שָׂרוּף עַל גַּבֵּי הַזֵּיתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's ruling from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that a burnt שרץ is טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats a burnt שרץ as unable to make the olives טמא, which implies a burnt שרץ is not טמא.

steps.title: רבי זירא: whole skeleton versus partial skeleton
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that ריש לקיש speaks of a burnt שרץ whose skeleton is entirely whole, while the משנה speaks of one where only part remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: This is not a difficulty. This one is about a case where all of it is there, and that one is about a case where only part of it is there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends ריש לקיש by showing that the two rulings speak about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A burnt שרץ is like a dry one, so it is טמא only when whole. ריש לקיש means a fully intact skeleton, which is טמא. The משנה's burnt שרץ is only partly intact, so it is טהור. Both rulings are true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a difficulty (the two sources speak of different cases)

steps.confusionAlert: This looks just like רבי זירא's answer in step 14, but there it answered a different challenge. Here the same whole-versus-part split protects ריש לקיש's ruling about a burnt שרץ.

phrases.english: רבי זירא said: It is not a difficulty —
this one is about all of them, that one is about part of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): whole versus partial
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say any burnt שרץ is טהור.
steps.terutzMaskana: A burnt שרץ with a fully intact skeleton is טמא. One that is only partly intact is טהור.

steps.title: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי is quoted again as support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי again. 'Them' might suggest only a whole שרץ counts, so the verse also says 'of them'. This shows that whole and part are separate categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יצחק son of רבי ביסנא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: The verse says 'them'. Might one think this applies only to whole ones? So the verse says 'of them'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the same ברייתא from step 15 again, this time as proof for רבי זירא's answer about a burnt שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's two words separate a whole שרץ from part of one. As the next step shows, this version matches 'them' (whole) to a burnt שרץ, so a burnt שרץ with an intact skeleton is טמא and a partial one is not. That is exactly רבי זירא's split.
steps.confusionAlert: The opening words match the ברייתא from steps 15-16, but watch the ending in the next step. There the two words are split as burnt versus not burnt, not moist versus dry.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
רבי יצחק son of רבי ביסנא said
in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי:
'Them' — might one think only when they are whole?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:31

phrases.english: So the verse says 'of them'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:32

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בְּרַבִּי בִּיסְנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רבי זירא's answer in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's split between a whole and a partial burnt שרץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי on 'בהם' and 'מהם'

steps.title: The ברייתא resolves the two verses: burnt versus not burnt
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the ברייתא says 'of them' alone would suggest even part counts, so the verse says 'them'. The two words are settled: a burnt שרץ must be whole, and a non-burnt שרץ is טמא even in part.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse only said 'of them', I might think even part of a שרץ makes things טמא. So the verse says 'them'. How do the two fit together? One verse is about a burnt שרץ, and the other is about one that is not burnt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it began in step 21. Its conclusion shows that 'whole' and 'part' are two separate rules, which supports רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the פסוק pulls a different way: 'them' points to a whole שרץ, and 'of them' points to part of one. The ברייתא gives each word its own case. A burnt שרץ needs to be whole (as ריש לקיש said), while a regular שרץ is טמא even if only part of it is touched. That is exactly the line רבי זירא drew between ריש לקיש and the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: part of them, a piece of the שרץ
the verse teaches (to rule out the mistaken idea)
how so? How do we fit these together?

steps.whatToRemember: A burnt שרץ is טמא only if it is whole (skeleton intact). A non-burnt שרץ is טמא even in part. This supports רבי זירא's answer and keeps ריש לקיש's ruling in place.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up which case is stricter. The burnt שרץ is the one that needs to be whole. The regular, unburnt שרץ is the one where even part of it makes things טמא.

phrases.english: If the verse said only 'of them,' I might think it applies even to part of them?
So the verse says 'them.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:31

phrases.english: How can both fit?
Here, it speaks of a burnt one,
phrases.notes: 'Them' (the whole thing) goes with the burnt שרץ.

phrases.english: there, of one that is not burnt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? כָּאן — בְּשָׂרוּף, כָּאן — בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׂרוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 21 and gives its resolution, which supports רבי זירא's answer in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's line between a whole burnt שרץ (טמא) and a partial one (not טמא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, which matches 'them' to a burnt שרץ and 'of them' to a non-burnt one.

steps.title: Why the זב and his fluids make things טמא only when moist
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that these items make things טמא only when moist. It gives the source for the זב's flow ('his flesh runs') and for his phlegm, mucus, and saliva ('if the זב spits', meaning like saliva).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They make things טמא when moist.' For the זב, it says 'his flesh runs', which means a wet flow. For his phlegm, mucus, and saliva, it says 'if the זב spits', so it must be like spit, which is wet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and starts giving a source for each item that is טמא only when moist. Here it covers the זב and the fluids from his mouth and nose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of each פסוק describe something wet. 'Runs' means flowing liquid, and 'spits' means saliva. So the טומאה applies only while the item is still in that wet state, not after it dries out.

keyTerms.meaning: a man with an abnormal discharge, who is טמא
similar to saliva, meaning wet like spit

phrases.english: They make things טמא when moist.
phrases.notes: These are the words of the משנה, which the גמרא is now explaining.

phrases.english: A זב — as it is written: 'his flesh runs,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:3

phrases.english: his phlegm, his mucus, and his saliva —
as it is written: 'if the זב spits,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:8

phrases.english: meaning something like saliva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the burnt שרץ discussion and starts explaining a new phrase from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זב's flow and his phlegm, mucus, and saliva make things טמא only when moist, as the פסוקים describe wet substances.

steps.title: Why the שרץ, semen, and נבלה make things טמא only when moist
steps.stepSummary: The שרץ makes things טמא 'when they are dead', meaning in a state like at death. Semen must be fit to fertilize. A נבלה is covered by 'if it dies', again meaning a state like at death.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a שרץ, the Torah says 'when they are dead', so it must be like it was when it died. Semen counts only if it can still fertilize. For a נבלה, it says 'if it dies', so again it must be like it was at death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list from the משנה and gives the reason for the remaining three items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the שרץ and the נבלה, 'like at death' means fresh and moist, as a body is when it first dies. For semen there is no פסוק, just a reason: it is טמא only while it could still fertilize, and dried semen cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: similar to the state at death, so still fresh and moist
the carcass of an animal that was not properly slaughtered

steps.whatToRemember: All five items in the משנה make things טמא only while moist. Each one has a reason: a wet flow, like spit, like at death, or still able to fertilize.

phrases.english: A שרץ — the Torah said 'when they are dead,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:31

phrases.english: meaning in a state like at death.
Semen that is fit to fertilize,
A נבלה — as it is written: 'if it dies' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39

phrases.english: meaning in a state like at death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources begun in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שרץ and a נבלה make things טמא only in a state like at death (moist). Semen makes things טמא only while it can still fertilize.

steps.title: Must the soaking water stay lukewarm the whole time?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says dried items can be soaked back to their earlier state. רבי ירמיה asks whether the water must be lukewarm from start to finish, or only at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If they can be soaked.' רבי ירמיה asked: does the soaking need lukewarm water from beginning to end, or is it enough that it starts lukewarm even if it is not lukewarm at the end?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about soaking dried items, and רבי ירמיה raises a question about exactly how the soaking test works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's test is whether a dried item can come back to its earlier state by soaking in lukewarm water. The question is how strict that test is: must the water stay lukewarm all along, or does starting lukewarm count even if it cools off? The next step answers this.

phrases.english: If they can be soaked.
phrases.notes: Back to the משנה: dried items that can be soaked back to their old state still make things טמא.

phrases.english: רבי ירמיה asked:
Must its beginning and its end be in lukewarm water,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא תְּחִילָּתוֹ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין סוֹפוֹ?
phrases.english: or perhaps just its beginning, even if not its end?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: תְּחִילָּתוֹ וְסוֹפוֹ בְּפוֹשְׁרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'moist' rule to the משנה's next clause about bringing dried items back by soaking.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the soaking test needs lukewarm water the entire time, or only at the start.

steps.title: How long the lukewarm soaking must last
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers רבי ירמיה. The soaking lasts a full day. יהודה בן נקוסא says the water only needs to be lukewarm at the start. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it must stay lukewarm the whole time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: How long is their soaking in lukewarm water? יהודה בן נקוסא says: a full twenty-four hours, and it is enough if the water is lukewarm at the start, even if it is not lukewarm at the end. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: the water must be lukewarm for the full twenty-four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that speaks directly to רבי ירמיה's question about lukewarm water. The ברייתא shows that both sides of his question are real opinions held by תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the soaking lasts a full day (מעת לעת). They argue about the water's temperature. יהודה בן נקוסא needs warmth only at the beginning, which matches the first side of רבי ירמיה's question. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs warmth from start to finish, which matches the other side.

keyTerms.term: תְּחִילָּתוֹ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין סוֹפוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: At its start, even if not at its end

steps.whatToRemember: The test soak lasts a full day. The only debate is whether the water must stay lukewarm the whole time.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
How much is their soaking in lukewarm water?
phrases.notes: 'Their' means the dried-out items from the משנה, which are soaked to see whether they can go back to how they were.

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּדָה בֶּן נָקוֹסָא אוֹמֵר: מֵעֵת לְעֵת,
phrases.english: Yehuda ben Nekosa says: a full twenty-four hours,

phrases.aramaic: תְּחִילָּתוֹ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין סוֹפוֹ.
phrases.english: lukewarm at its start, even though not at its end.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
They must be lukewarm for the full twenty-four hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question from Step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must the soaking water be lukewarm from start to finish, or only at the start?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: This is a dispute between תנאים. יהודה בן נקוסא needs warmth only at the start. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs it for the full twenty-four hours.

steps.title: שמואל explains רבי יוסי on dried corpse flesh
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי calls dried corpse flesh טהור. שמואל explains that this only means it no longer makes things טמא as a כזית. It still carries טומאת רקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that רבי יוסי says: the flesh of a corpse, etc. שמואל said: It is טהור in that it no longer makes things טמא as an olive-sized piece, but it still makes things טמא with the טומאה of רקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, where רבי יוסי says dried corpse flesh is טהור. שמואל limits how far that 'טהור' goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כזית of corpse flesh makes things טמא. Once the flesh has dried and cannot be restored, it loses that כזית-level טומאה. Still, it does not become fully טהור. It falls into a different category, טומאת רקב, the טומאה of a corpse's decayed remains.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-sized amount, the usual minimum amount of corpse flesh that makes things טמא
The טומאה of the decayed remains of a corpse
Pure in the sense of not making other things טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי יוסי's 'טהור' as fully pure. According to שמואל, it only loses one level of טומאה, the כזית level.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בְּשַׂר הַמֵּת כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: the flesh of a corpse, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the opening of רבי יוסי's line in our משנה. 'Etc.' points to the rest: dried flesh that cannot be restored is טהור.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
It is pure from making things impure as an olive-bulk,
but it makes things impure with the impurity of decay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dried corpse flesh does not make things טמא as a כזית, but it does carry טומאת רקב.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי himself saying exactly what שמואל said. Dried corpse flesh is טהור from כזית-level טומאה but is still טמא with טומאת רקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי says: the flesh of a corpse that dried up and cannot be soaked and go back to how it was is טהור in that it no longer makes things טמא as a כזית, but it is טמא with the טומאה of רקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up שמואל's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל was explaining what רבי יוסי meant. Here a ברייתא has רבי יוסי saying the same two-part rule in so many words. This shows שמואל's reading is correct. The ברייתא also spells out the case: the flesh cannot be soaked back to its earlier state.

keyTerms.meaning: To be soaked and return to its earlier state

steps.whatToRemember: Dried corpse flesh that cannot be restored loses its כזית-level טומאה, but it still has טומאת רקב.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בְּשַׂר הַמֵּת שֶׁיָּבַשׁ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: the flesh of a corpse that dried up

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין יָכוֹל לִשְׁרוֹת וְלַחֲזוֹר כְּמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה —
phrases.english: and cannot be soaked and go back to how it was —
is pure from making things impure as an olive-bulk,
but is impure with the impurity of decay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's statement in Step 27.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's explanation that dried corpse flesh still carries טומאת רקב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוסי states the same two-part rule.

steps.title: A שרץ found in an alleyway makes things טמא back in time
steps.stepSummary: New משנה. A שרץ found in an alleyway makes things טמא back in time. This goes back to the last time someone checked the alleyway and found no שרץ, or to the last time it was swept.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A שרץ that is found in an alleyway makes things טמא back in time. This goes back to when one can say, 'I checked this alleyway and there was no שרץ in it,' or back to the time it was swept.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that when a שרץ is found, we assume it may have been there for a while, so anything that passed through the alleyway is affected back in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know when the שרץ arrived, so the טומאה reaches back in time (למפרע). It does not go back forever. It stops at the last moment we know the alleyway was clear: either a real check, or a sweeping. The גמרא in step 32 asks exactly why a sweeping counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule of retroactive טומאה that the משנה applies next to a כתם on a garment.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A creeping creature that is found in an alleyway —
makes things impure retroactively,
phrases.notes: He means the pure items that passed through the alleyway during that time.

phrases.english: back to the time when one can say:
"I checked this alleyway
and there was no creeping creature in it,"
or back to the time of sweeping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שרץ found in an alleyway makes things טמא back in time, until the last check or sweeping.

steps.title: A stain found on a garment makes things טמא back in time
steps.stepSummary: The same rule applies to a כתם found on a woman's garment. It makes her טמא back in time, until the last check of the garment or the last time it was laundered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, a stain found on a garment makes things טמא back in time. This goes back to when she can say, 'I checked this garment and there was no stain on it,' or back to the time it was laundered.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same back-in-time rule to a blood stain on a woman's garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with the שרץ, we do not know when the stain appeared, so the טומאה reaches back. The cut-off point is the last time the garment is known to have been clean: a check, or a laundering, which would have removed any earlier stain.
steps.whatToRemember: A שרץ in an alleyway and a כתם on a garment follow one rule: the טומאה goes back in time, but only until the last check or cleaning.

phrases.english: And likewise, a stain that is found on a garment —
phrases.notes: The garment belongs to a woman, and the stain is a blood stain.

phrases.english: makes things impure retroactively,
back to the time when one can say: "I checked this garment
and there was no stain on it,"
or back to the time of laundering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from Step 29 to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כתם found on a garment makes things טמא back in time, until the last check or laundering.

steps.title: Moist or dry: how far back the טומאה reaches
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the שרץ or כתם makes things טמא back in time whether it is moist or dry. רבי שמעון says a dry one goes back in time, but a moist one only goes back as far as it could still be moist.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes things טמא whether it is moist or dry. רבי שמעון says: a dry one makes things טמא back in time. A moist one only makes things טמא back to a time from which it could still be moist now.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its rule about a שרץ in an alleyway and a כתם on a garment. It adds a disagreement about whether being moist or dry changes how far back the טומאה goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the condition of the item makes no difference: we go all the way back to the last check or sweeping either way. רבי שמעון says a moist item shows it got there recently. So we only go back to the time from which it could have stayed moist until now.

keyTerms.meaning: Back in time, going backwards from now

phrases.english: And it makes things impure whether it is moist or dry.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the שרץ or the כתם from the earlier part of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The dry one makes things impure back in time,
but the moist one does not make things impure
except back to a time
from which it could still be moist.
phrases.notes: He means: only as far back as it could have sat there and still be wet now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in steps 29-30 by adding the moist/dry disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: moist or dry, it makes things טמא back to the last check or sweeping. רבי שמעון: a moist one only goes back to when it could still be moist.

steps.title: Why does sweeping mark the cutoff?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'until the time of sweeping.' Is a swept alleyway treated as checked, or as cleared of everything?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They asked: 'Until the time of sweeping.' Do we assume the alleyway was checked? Or do we assume it was swept clean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the משנה's words 'until the time of sweeping.' It wants to know why sweeping clears the time before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible reasons. Maybe whoever swept looked the place over, so he would have seen a שרץ (חזקתו בדוק). Or maybe the sweeping itself pushed out anything lying there (חזקתו מתכבד).

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before the חכמים
A presumption, what we assume is true

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that sweeping clears the earlier time. They only argue about why: because it was checked, or because it was cleared out.

phrases.english: Gemara: A question was asked before them:
"Until the time of sweeping":
phrases.notes: These are the words of the משנה from step 29.

phrases.english: is its presumption that it was checked,
or perhaps its presumption is that it was swept clean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by asking about a phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why sweeping clears the time before it: is the alleyway assumed checked, or assumed swept clean?

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask whether the question matters in practice. This sets up the next step, where it shows a case that comes out differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually both reasons lead to the same result, since sweeping normally includes looking. So the גמרא needs a case where the two reasons split apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference comes out of this?

phrases.english: And what practical difference comes out of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the question in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where 'checked' and 'swept clean' would give different results.

steps.title: Swept but not checked
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up when the sweeper says he swept but did not check. If the reason is checking, this alleyway is not cleared. If the reason is sweeping, it is cleared.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he said: 'I swept, but I did not check.' If you say the presumption is that it was checked, here it was not checked. If you say the presumption is that it was swept, here it was swept.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a case: someone swept the alleyway but says he did not look it over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If sweeping counts only because it includes looking, then here nobody looked, so the earlier time is not cleared. If sweeping counts because it clears things out, then this alleyway was still swept, so the earlier time is cleared. The question itself stays open here.
steps.whatToRemember: Sweeping may count because it is a check, or because it clears the area. The difference is a case of swept but not checked.

phrases.english: Where he said: "It was swept but not checked."
If you say its presumption is that it was checked,
this one was not checked,
if you say its presumption is that it was swept clean,
this one was swept clean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33 by giving the case where the two reasons split.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the sweeper says he swept but did not check: under 'checked' the earlier time is not cleared, and under 'swept' it is cleared.
